clue.text: The new stadium designed for them?

definitions.text: The new stadium designed for them?

indicators.note: something designed is laid out afresh, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new football ground has been built with a particular club in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges THE NEW STADIUM into the club's name; the whole clue also describes the club's move to London's Olympic-era stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The London football club is a team for whom a new home ground could be built.

clue.text: Seizing smack, we arrest for sort of crime

indicators.note: seizing means holding, so the word we wraps around the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
to smack is to hit
to collar someone is police slang for arresting them

explanation.surface: Officers confess they nab people for a certain kind of offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud and embezzlement by office workers are classed as this kind of offence.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: broken off means the end of the word is snapped away, losing its final letter

parts.note: a horseshoe nail is driven into a horse's hoof

explanation.surface: A horse rears up and a shoe nail snaps off in its hoof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' turns IS into SI; 'broken off' cuts the last letter from NAIL, leaving NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is the mountain where Moses received the commandments.

parts.note: Num is the short form of Numbers, a book of the Bible
to say 'ah' is to sound surprised

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise goes with flicking through one scripture or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bare word 'another': another holy book besides Numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets, a book of the Old Testament, so a further holy book.

clue.text: Two players taking up Arabic lute …

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means lifting, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: the oud is a lute played across the Arab world

explanation.surface: A pair of musicians pick up an Arabic stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' reverses OUD in this down clue. The ellipsis leads on to 12-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of musicians performing together is a duo.

clue.text: Phineas, not fat for an EastEnder, say

indicators.note: a Cockney from London's East End says 'th' as 'f', so the word is pronounced with an F

parts.note: not fat means thin

explanation.surface: A man named Phineas is told he is slim in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech turns THIN into 'fin'. Phineas Finn is the hero of Trollope's political novel of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Phineas Finn is the Irish MP who gives Trollope's novel its title, so the first name points to the surname.

clue.text: Weed has to stay at school

parts.note: to stay is to rest or remain
Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the weeds must remain at boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a famous fee-paying school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Restharrow is a tough-rooted wild plant of the pea family, a weed of fields.

clue.text: Likely to lose, then? It's a possibility

indicators.note: a possibility is one possible arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders if they are about to lose and concedes it might happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: By the proverb, someone who wavers and delays tends to lose out.

clue.text: American port not always in the same place?

definitions.meaning: the Alabama city on the Gulf of Mexico

definitions.text: not always in the same place?

explanation.definitionFit: Mobile, Alabama is a Gulf Coast port, and the adjective means movable.

clue.text: … fast come to prefer flutes, etc

parts.note: to come to like something is to prefer it
flutes, oboes and clarinets make up the wind section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A musical pair grows to favour the woodwind instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues from 7-down's ellipsis; 'fast' opens this clue as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To go like the wind is an idiom for moving very quickly.

clue.text: Follower of Brutus is no brute, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, haphazard way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One of Brutus's men is said to be quite gentle, at any rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges IS NO BRUTE; the surface plays on the 'Et tu, Brute' story.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebonius was one of the conspirators who joined Brutus in killing Julius Caesar.

clue.text: New commander-in-chief's victory

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, Allied supreme commander

explanation.surface: A newly appointed military leader wins a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike was the Greek goddess personifying victory.

clue.text: Dry piece of writing gets bad mark

definitions.meaning: to soak up wet ink from a written page with absorbent paper
a stain or a blemish on one's record

explanation.definitionFit: To blot is to dry fresh ink, and a blot is a smudge or a stain on a reputation.

clue.text: Proposed well-cooked English meal; no alternative

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it for discussion
food that is well cooked is served hot

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a thoroughly cooked English dinner, take it or leave it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage to 'table' a motion is to put it forward; in the US it means the opposite, to shelve it.
explanation.definitionFit: A table d'hote is a fixed-price set menu, offering diners no choice of dishes.

clue.text: Give name, but mean to conceal tip-off

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so mean wraps around the jumbled word

parts.note: mean in the sense of low or ignoble is base

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of tip are jumbled

explanation.surface: Christening a child, yet meaning to keep a warning quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-off' looks like one word meaning a warning, but it splits: 'tip' is the fodder and 'off' its jumbling signal, while 'to conceal' puts the result inside the word for mean.
explanation.definitionFit: To baptise someone is to christen them, giving a name at the ceremony.

clue.text: In summary, where USSR came historically?

parts.note: came earlier in history, before something: pre-
the USSR was succeeded by the CIS, the Commonwealth of Independent States, so the Soviet Union came before the CIS

explanation.surface: A brief history question asks where the Soviet Union stood in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Soviet Union came before (pre) the CIS, the loose union of former Soviet states formed in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: A precis is a short abstract or condensed account of a text.

clue.text: Succeeded, very tired, getting confirmed in office

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
worn out, worn, means very tired

explanation.surface: A weary successor is finally installed in a post.
explanation.definitionFit: An official is sworn in by taking an oath on entering office.

clue.text: Reminder to be ready earlier

definitions.meaning: one who reminds actors of forgotten lines
more prompt, quicker to act or arrive

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's prompter cues forgotten lines, and the comparative adjective means more punctual.

clue.text: Genuine wrinkle, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard spoken, so the word is the sound of another

parts.note: to pucker is to wrinkle or crease

explanation.surface: Someone insists a crease is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: PUKKA, from Hindi, is British slang for genuine or first-class; in non-rhotic speech it sounds like PUCKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka, a borrowing from Hindi, means authentic or the real thing.

clue.text: Girl's old party skirt: having a date, she may put it on

definitions.text: having a date, she may put it on

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a do is a party
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A girl dresses in her old party miniskirt for a date.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on dates in the year of our Lord and on 'putting on' years as one ages; 'Anno Domini' is also a jokey term for old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates are written with AD, and as years pass a woman puts on age, also called this.

clue.text: My name's come up: I'll be hanged

indicators.note: in a down clue come up means rising, so the pieces read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name; that the reversed run also sits inside the words 'My name' is a coincidence of this reading

explanation.surface: Someone sees their name called and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' reverses MY + N. Nym is a thief in Shakespeare's Henry V who is hanged, as reported in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Nym, Falstaff's crony, is hanged for theft during the French campaign in Henry V.

clue.text: Dagger rips short skirt

indicators.note: rips means tears apart, so the remaining letters are jumbled
short means cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blade slashes through a miniskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts SKIRT to SKIR, and 'rips' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Separate in fog, and fail to get clear

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the next

parts.note: mist is a light fog
to sunder is to separate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people part ways in fog and cannot see where they are going.
explanation.definitionFit: To misunderstand is to fail to grasp something, so a point is not made clear.
